profile.name: Tagbilaran City Waterworks System
profile.operator: LGU-operated waterworks, local economic enterprise (LEE), reports to the mayor
profile.city: Tagbilaran City, Bohol: 15 barangays (12 urban), population 106,120 (2024 census)
profile.service_area: 10 of 15 barangays (Bool, Booy, Cabawan, Cogon, Dao, Manga, San Isidro, Taloto, Tiptip, Ubujan); about 82,500 people
profile.water_source: Groundwater only, 28 deep-well pumping stations (160.5 HP), chlorination
profile.other_providers: BWUI (15,040 connections) and Richli Water (bulk surface water) also serve the city

module2.vision_previous: To manage our organization and water resources to meet evolving regulatory requirements, water supply needs, and customer expectations in the future.
module2.mission_previous: Our mission is to provide our customers with safe and reliable water in compliance with regulatory requirements. We strive to treat every customer fairly and respectfully, and to address their needs quickly and effectively.
module2.vision: We want to become a world-class, sustainable waterworks by 2035. We want to achieve highly potable, 24/7 water supply. We see a more effective waterworks company capable of providing reliable and safe/clean water to every household in Tagbilaran City.
module2.mission: Our mission is to provide our customers in 10/15 barangays in Tagbilaran City with safe and reliable water. Our employees are capable and highly trained. We strive to treat every customer fairly and respectfully and address their needs quickly and effectively.

narratives.Commercial: Connections grew from 5,612 (2020) to 6,461 (2024); billed volume stayed between 1.70 and 1.90 million m3 per year. Collections rose from PhP 18.7 M to 23.1 M (2023) and dipped in 2024. The tariff is unchanged since 2016, so revenue per billed m3 is about PhP 12.
narratives.Technical: All water comes from 28 deep-well pumping stations with chlorination. NRW fell from about 46% (2023) to 31% (H1 2025), partly because production fell from 3.5 to 3.0 million m3. Supply is 22-24 hours a day.
narratives.Financial: OPEX rose from PhP 17.1 M (2020) to 26.1 M (2023, calculated), above collections from 2023 (operating ratio 1.13). The should-be tariff to recover OPEX was PhP 17.68/m3 in 2024.
narratives.Human talent: 24 staff (9 regular, 15 job order); multi-tasking and training needs flagged in the SWOT.
narratives._note: Draft narratives written from the source data; TCWS team to validate.

demographics.implications: Households grow about 1.6% a year; TCWS serves a third of its service area; once provincial bulk water arrives (assumed 2030) TCWS stops deep wells and must serve a net demand of about 18 MLD.

pillars.assessment: Draft Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) sets KPI standards for LGU-run waterworks; mayor states TCWS will not be privatized.
TCWS reports directly to the mayor; three WSPs serve the city (TCWS, BWUI, Richli).
Provincial bulk water supply project; collaboration with BWUI; DILG provincial and regional support; DPWH AWSPSA.
LEE, not funded by general funds; CAPEX modeled as 100% grant; tariff unchanged since 2016.
PNSDW water quality standards; monthly bacteriological testing; septage facilities (JICA pilot 24 m3/day, planned 25-100 m3/day).

enablement_environment.sanitation: Households with basic sanitation reported as 103% by PPDO (May 2024) - data quality issue.
enablement_environment.rating_gap: Ratings 1-5 to be set by the team

strengths: Already under a local economic enterprise (LEE), not funded by general funds
Installed chlorinators in all pumping stations
Responsive team, especially in emergency services
weaknesses: Old galvanized iron pipes (parts of Brgys. Tiptip, Manga, Ubujan)
Need training for technical and finance personnel
Lack of training for billing and collection, management, water safety plans
Water quality monitoring and compliance (10% failure in sampling)
opportunities: Availability of bulk water supply in a few years' time
NGOs and private organizations (e.g. USAID, Maynilad) that help improve water supply
Other local water utilities' support (collaboration with BWUI)
threats: Natural hazards (typhoons, earthquakes); standby gensets in selected pumping stations
Deep-well sources of some private institutions, establishments and businesses

strategies.title: Expansion to unserved areas
tasks: Extend pipelines to Brgys. Cabawan, Booy, Cogon, Dampas, Bool
Construct new reservoirs in the expansion areas

tasks: Conduct pump testing
Assess and upgrade some of the existing pump units
Regularly maintain pump stations, chlorinators and gensets

strategies.title: Identification and replacement of old and inaccurate meters
tasks: Procure water meters for new consumers; recalibrate or replace meters of existing customers (meters are currently provided by consumers)

strategies.title: Identify illegal connections
tasks: Hire or designate more people to investigate illegal connections
Improve the expertise of employees

strategies.title: Identify problematic old pipes / high physical NRW
tasks: Establish 6 DMAs covering all TCWS service areas
Replace old pipes at Brgys. Manga, Ubujan, Taloto
Appoint and train personnel to operate the DMAs

strategies.title: Disconnection enforcement
tasks: Review or revisit the service contracts
Establish baseline data

strategies.title: Staggered payments
tasks: Establish a staggered accounts-receivable payment schedule
Establish policies on accounts receivable

strategies.title: Set up an LEE with ring-fenced accounts
tasks: Ring-fence the waterworks account
Regularly evaluate job designations and descriptions

strategies.title: OPEX efficiency
tasks: Develop and implement energy-efficiency measures (fuel and electricity)
Regularly monitor fuel and electricity unit costs

strategies.title: Formalize customer service standards
tasks: No-water complaints: simple 24-48 h, complex 5-7 working days
Mainline leak reports: within 24 h
Illegal tapping: investigate within 2 days, charge penalty, connect meters
Customer bulletins: daily during emergencies, inform barangay leaders, promote Facebook page
New applications: inspect within 24-48 h, approve within 7 working days, payment then installation
